items.jp: さあ、ボートから降りて岸まで泳ぎなさい。

translation.pt-BR: Vamos, desce do barco e nada até a margem.
translation.en: Now, get off the boat and swim to shore.

items.label: particle of origin/starting point
items.explanation: から marca ボート como o ponto de onde se desce: é do barco que a pessoa deve sair.

items.jp: 家から遠くないところにあるのは軍の病院です。

translation.pt-BR: O que fica perto de casa é um hospital militar.
translation.en: Not far from the house was a military hospital.

items.label: particle of origin/starting point
items.explanation: から marca 家 como o ponto a partir do qual a distância é medida: 'não longe de casa'.

items.jp: この間、君からＦＡＸが届いた。

translation.pt-BR: Outro dia chegou um fax seu.
translation.en: I got your fax the other day.

items.label: particle of origin/starting point
items.explanation: から here marks WHERE (or whom) something comes from: 君から = 'from you.' It indicates the source of the fax.

items.jp: ここから波の音が聞こえる。

translation.pt-BR: Daqui dá para ouvir o barulho das ondas.
translation.en: The sea can be heard from here.

items.label: particle of origin/starting point
items.explanation: から marca ここ como o ponto de onde o som chega: é daqui que as ondas se ouvem.

items.jp: このため、今夜から明日にかけて全般に曇りや雨の天気でしょう。

translation.pt-BR: Por causa disso, de hoje à noite até amanhã o tempo deve ficar, no geral, nublado e chuvoso.
translation.en: Because of this it will probably be generally cloudy and rainy weather over tonight and tomorrow.

items.label: particle of origin/starting point
items.explanation: から marca 今夜 ('hoje à noite') como o início da previsão.

items.jp: 瓶から飲まないでください。

translation.pt-BR: Por favor, não beba direto da garrafa.
translation.en: Please don't drink from the bottle.

items.label: particle of origin/starting point
items.explanation: から marca 瓶 como o ponto de onde a bebida sairia: beber direto da garrafa é justamente o que se pede que não se faça.

items.jp: 予算から2千円足が出た。

translation.pt-BR: Estouramos o orçamento em dois mil ienes.
translation.en: We ran over the budget by two thousand yen.

items.label: particle of origin/starting point
items.explanation: から marca 予算 como o ponto a partir do qual a conta passou: o estouro é medido do orçamento para cima.

items.jp: 父は病気から回復した。

translation.pt-BR: Meu pai se recuperou da doença.
translation.en: My father got well again.

items.label: particle of origin/starting point
items.explanation: から marca 病気 como o ponto de onde ele saiu: a recuperação parte da doença.

items.jp: 泥棒から盗むのは罪じゃない。

translation.pt-BR: Roubar de um ladrão não é crime.
translation.en: It's no crime to steal from a thief.

items.label: particle of origin/starting point
items.explanation: から marca 泥棒 como a origem do roubo: é dele que se tira a coisa.

items.jp: 今日は大勢の客が来た

translation.pt-BR: Hoje vieram muitos clientes.
translation.en: A lot of people (a lot of customers) came today.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 大勢の客 (many customers) as the ones who performed the action of coming; it presents the subject neutrally.

items.jp: 月がとても丸い

translation.pt-BR: A lua está bem redonda.
translation.en: The moon is really round.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 月 as the subject being described; が (not は) is used to introduce or highlight the observed characteristic of the moon.

items.jp: 彼は細かいことが気になる

translation.pt-BR: Ele se incomoda com os mínimos detalhes.
translation.en: He worries about small details.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 細かいこと as the thing that 'stays on one's mind'. In the expression 気になる, what bothers/draws attention is marked by が.
tokens: part of the expression 気になる

items.jp: 花瓶が窓のそばにあります

translation.pt-BR: Tem um vaso perto da janela.
translation.en: There's a vase near the window.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 花瓶 as the subject that exists; with verbs of existence (ある) one uses が, not は, to present something new.

items.jp: 坂の上に古いお寺がある

translation.pt-BR: No alto da ladeira tem um templo antigo.
translation.en: At the top of the slope there's an old temple.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 古いお寺 (old temple) as the thing that exists. In existence sentences with ある, what exists is presented with が.

items.jp: 服に犬の毛がついている

translation.pt-BR: Tem pelo de cachorro grudado na roupa.
translation.en: There's dog hair stuck to my clothes.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 毛 (fur) as what is stuck, presenting it as new information.

items.jp: 机の上に本やペンがある

translation.pt-BR: Em cima da mesa tem livros, canetas e coisas assim.
translation.en: On the table there are things like books and pens.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 本やペン as that which exists; with ある, what appears is typically marked by が.

items.jp: 机の上に字引がある

translation.pt-BR: Tem um dicionário em cima da mesa.
translation.en: There's a dictionary on the desk.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 字引 (dictionary) as what exists. In existence sentences, what exists comes with が.

items.jp: 兄弟はとても仲がいい

translation.pt-BR: Os irmãos se dão muito bem.
translation.en: The siblings get along very well.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 仲 as the subject of the adjective いい within the expression 仲がいい ('the relationship is good'), which describes the topic.
tokens: subject (part of the expression 仲がいい)

items.jp: 字が細かくて読めない

translation.pt-BR: A letra é tão pequena que não dá pra ler.
translation.en: The letters are so small I can't read them.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 字 (the writing) as the subject that gives rise to the situation: it is the writing that is tiny. Here が, and not は, because it presents a concrete fact of the immediate situation.

items.jp: 二つの国の貿易が増えました

translation.pt-BR: O comércio entre os dois países aumentou.
translation.en: Trade between the two countries has increased.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: Marks 貿易 (trade) as the subject performing the action of increasing. が is used to present a new fact/phenomenon.

items.jp: 卵が三つ残っている

translation.pt-BR: Restam três ovos.
translation.en: There are three eggs left.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 卵 as the subject in the described state, presenting it as new/observed information.

items.jp: 二つの店が競争している

translation.pt-BR: As duas lojas estão competindo entre si.
translation.en: The two stores are competing with each other.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 二つの店 as the subject that performs the action of competing.
tokens: nominal head of the compound verb

items.jp: 祭りでは美しい花火が見られる

translation.pt-BR: No festival dá pra ver belos fogos de artifício.
translation.en: At the festival you can see beautiful fireworks.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 花火 as the grammatical subject of the potential verb 見られる: it is the fireworks that 'can be seen'.

items.jp: テーブルの上に杯が並んでいる

translation.pt-BR: Há várias taças enfileiradas em cima da mesa.
translation.en: There are several cups lined up on the table.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が introduces 杯 as the subject that is lined up; が is used because it describes the existence/situation of something new in the scene.

items.jp: 祭りで着物を着る人が多い

translation.pt-BR: Tem muita gente que usa quimono nas festas.
translation.en: A lot of people wear kimono at festivals.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 着物を着る人 as the subject of 多い; with 多い/少ない, what exists in quantity takes が.
tokens: verb of the relative clause (modifies 人)

items.jp: 夜は星がよく見られる

translation.pt-BR: À noite dá para ver bem as estrelas.
translation.en: At night you can see the stars clearly.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 星 as what can be seen; with the potential form, the object usually comes with が.

items.jp: 町の灯がきれいに見える

translation.pt-BR: As luzes da cidade ficam lindas de ver.
translation.en: The lights of the town look beautiful.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca 灯 como o sujeito de きれい, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: 転んで足から血が出た

translation.pt-BR: Caí e meu pé começou a sangrar.
translation.en: I fell and my foot started bleeding.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 血 (blood) as the subject of the verb 出る (that which came out).

items.jp: 冷蔵庫にビールが冷やしてある

translation.pt-BR: Tem cerveja gelando na geladeira.
translation.en: There's beer chilling in the fridge.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks ビール as the thing that is in the resultant state of having been set to chill.
tokens: subject (thing that is in the resulting state)
main verb in the て form

items.jp: みんなが元気でいるように祈ります

translation.pt-BR: Torço para que todo mundo continue bem de saúde.
translation.en: I hope everyone stays healthy.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks みんな as the subject that 'is well' within the clause 元気でいる.

items.jp: あの猫は足が細い

translation.pt-BR: Aquele gato tem as patas finas.
translation.en: That cat has thin legs.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 足 (the paws) as the specific subject that receives the description 'slender'. In the は...が pattern, が highlights exactly which part has the characteristic.

items.jp: テーブルの上に灰皿がある

translation.pt-BR: Tem um cinzeiro em cima da mesa.
translation.en: There's an ashtray on the table.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が introduces 灰皿 as what exists; with ある, が is used to introduce what is present in the place.

items.jp: この山は緑がきれいです

translation.pt-BR: Neste monte, o verde é bonito.
translation.en: On this mountain, the greenery is beautiful.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 緑 as the subject possessing the described quality (きれい), within the comment about the topic 山.

items.jp: おばあさんがお菓子をくれた

translation.pt-BR: A vovó me deu uns docinhos.
translation.en: Grandma gave me some sweets.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks the grandmother as the one who performs the action of giving; with the verb くれる, she is the giver.

items.jp: 学生の頃はお金がなかった

translation.pt-BR: Na época em que eu era estudante eu não tinha dinheiro.
translation.en: Back when I was a student, I didn't have any money.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks お金 as the subject of the existence predicate; with ない/なかった it indicates what was lacking: 'money (was what) there was none of'.

items.jp: この店には灰皿がない

translation.pt-BR: Neste estabelecimento não tem cinzeiro.
translation.en: There's no ashtray at this establishment.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 灰皿 as that whose existence is being denied; with ある/ない, が is used for the item present or absent, not は.
tokens: demonstrative adjective (連体詞 modifying 店)

items.jp: 大臣が記者に接見しました

translation.pt-BR: O ministro recebeu os jornalistas em audiência.
translation.en: The minister received the journalists in an audience.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 大臣 as the one who performs the action of receiving in audience; here it presents the subject as new/neutral information, not as an already-known topic.
tokens: target of the action (who is received)
nominal stem of the compound verb

items.jp: 鼻から血が出て、びっくりした

translation.pt-BR: Saiu sangue do nariz e eu levei um susto.
translation.en: Blood came out of my nose and it startled me.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 血 (blood) as what performs the action of coming out, presenting it as new information.

items.jp: 電話番号に零が二つあります

translation.pt-BR: No número de telefone tem dois zeros.
translation.en: There are two zeros in the phone number.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 零 ('zero') as that whose existence is asserted. In the 'に...が...あります' pattern, が points to what exists at the location.

items.jp: 卵が二つ残っています

translation.pt-BR: Sobraram dois ovos.
translation.en: Two eggs are left over.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 卵 (eggs) as that which is in the state of 'being left over'; intransitive verbs like 残る take the subject with が.

items.jp: 駅の近くに二階建てのバスがある

translation.pt-BR: Perto da estação tem um ônibus de dois andares.
translation.en: There's a double-decker bus near the station.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks バス as that which exists; with ある, the subject of existence takes が.

items.jp: 母の病気が早く治るように祈った

translation.pt-BR: Rezei para que a doença da minha mãe sarasse logo.
translation.en: I prayed that my mother's illness would get better soon.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 病気 as the subject that 'heals' within the clause 早く治る.

items.jp: 店の前に人がたくさん並んでいる

translation.pt-BR: Tem um monte de gente na fila na frente da loja.
translation.en: There's a long line of people in front of the store.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 人 as the subject performing/being in the state of the action; it is typical to introduce new information (there are people there) with が.

items.jp: 彼は料理の技術が高い

translation.pt-BR: Ele tem uma técnica de cozinha excelente.
translation.en: He has excellent cooking skills.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 料理の技術 as the grammatical subject of the adjective 高い. In the structure 〜は〜が〜, は gives the broad topic and が points to the specific property that is 'high'.

items.jp: 午後から空が曇りました

translation.pt-BR: A partir da tarde o céu ficou nublado.
translation.en: From the afternoon on, the sky got cloudy.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 空 as the subject of the described phenomenon, presenting it as new information.

items.jp: 公園に大勢の人がいる

translation.pt-BR: Tem muita gente no parque.
translation.en: There are a lot of people in the park.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 大勢の人 (many people) as that which exists; with existence verbs the subject takes が, not は.

items.jp: 糸が切れてしまった

translation.pt-BR: O fio acabou arrebentando.
translation.en: The thread ended up snapping.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 糸 ('thread') as the subject that undergoes the event. が (and not は) is used because it is a fact/event being observed, emphasizing what happened to the thread.
tokens: auxiliary (補助動詞) of the 〜てしまう construction

items.jp: この部屋は畳が古いです

translation.pt-BR: Neste quarto, o tatame é velho.
translation.en: In this room, the tatami is old.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 畳 (the tatami) as the specific subject described as old, within the topic 'this room'.

items.jp: 畳の部屋はいいにおいがします

translation.pt-BR: O quarto de tatame tem um cheiro bom.
translation.en: The tatami room has a nice smell.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks いいにおい (a nice smell) as the subject in the set expression においがする (to give off/sense a smell).

items.jp: 靴の中に砂が入った

translation.pt-BR: Entrou areia dentro do sapato.
translation.en: Sand got inside my shoe.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 砂 (sand) as what entered. が is used because it reports a new/observed event, with no prior topic.

items.jp: 雨の日は車がすぐ汚れる

translation.pt-BR: Em dia de chuva o carro fica sujo rapidinho.
translation.en: On rainy days the car gets dirty quickly.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 車 (car) as the subject that undergoes the change of state expressed by 汚れる, in contrast with the topic marked by は.

items.jp: 夏は薄いシャツがいい

translation.pt-BR: No verão é melhor uma camisa fininha.
translation.en: In summer a thin shirt is better.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks シャツ as that which is いい. With adjectives like いい (being good/preferable), が points to the chosen item as the ideal one.

items.jp: 服が泥で汚れてしまった

translation.pt-BR: A roupa acabou ficando toda suja de lama.
translation.en: My clothes ended up all covered in mud.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 服 (clothes) as the subject of the event; with change-of-state verbs like 汚れる, が points to what undergoes the change.

items.jp: この港から貿易が始まりました

translation.pt-BR: O comércio começou a partir deste porto.
translation.en: Trade began from this port.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: Marks 貿易 (trade) as the subject of the verb 始まる (to begin). With the intransitive 始まる, が is used for what begins.

items.jp: 今日は天気がいいから洗濯しよう

translation.pt-BR: Hoje o tempo está bom, então vou lavar roupa.
translation.en: The weather is nice today, so I'm going to do the laundry.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 天気 (the weather) as the subject of the adjective いい: it is the weather that is good.

items.jp: 箱の中に卵が五つある

translation.pt-BR: Dentro da caixa tem cinco ovos.
translation.en: There are five eggs inside the box.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 卵 (egg) as the subject that exists. In existence sentences with ある, what exists is pointed to by が.

items.jp: 旅行が楽しくなるように祈っている

translation.pt-BR: Estou torcendo para que a viagem seja divertida.
translation.en: I'm hoping the trip will be fun.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 旅行 as the subject that 'becomes fun' within the clause 楽しくなる.

items.jp: 子どもたちが門の前で並んだ

translation.pt-BR: As crianças ficaram em fila na frente do portão.
translation.en: The children lined up in front of the gate.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 子どもたち as who performs the action of lining up.

items.jp: 財布にお金がありません

translation.pt-BR: Não tem dinheiro na carteira.
translation.en: There's no money in the wallet.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks お金 as the subject whose existence is asserted or denied; with ある/ありません one uses が, not は.

items.jp: 先生が新しい本を紹介した

translation.pt-BR: O professor apresentou um livro novo.
translation.en: The teacher introduced a new book.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 先生 as the subject that performs the action of introducing/recommending.
tokens: nominal stem of the compound verb

items.jp: 子供の手が汚れています

translation.pt-BR: As mãos da criança estão sujas.
translation.en: The child's hands are dirty.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 手 (hands) as what is in the state of being dirty. が is used (and not は) because it neutrally describes an observed condition, without highlighting a topic.

items.jp: まだ先生から連絡がない

translation.pt-BR: O professor ainda não deu notícias.
translation.en: The teacher still hasn't been in touch.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 連絡 as the subject of the negated existence; with ない/ある, が is used to indicate what does (not) exist.

items.jp: 春の原には花がたくさん咲く

translation.pt-BR: Na primavera, muitas flores desabrocham no campo.
translation.en: Many flowers bloom in the spring fields.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca 花 como o sujeito de 咲く, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: 細かいお金がありますか

translation.pt-BR: Você tem dinheiro trocado?
translation.en: Do you have any small change?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 細かいお金 as the subject of ある. With existence verbs like ある, what exists is normally marked by が.

items.jp: 市長との接見が決まりました

translation.pt-BR: Ficou marcada a audiência com o prefeito.
translation.en: The meeting with the mayor was scheduled.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 接見 as the subject of 決まる; with intransitive verbs of 'becoming decided' one uses が, since something simply comes to happen.

items.jp: この町では古いお寺が見られる

translation.pt-BR: Nesta cidade dá pra ver templos antigos.
translation.en: In this town you can see old temples.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks お寺 as the grammatical subject of the potential verb 見られる: it is the temple that 'can be seen'.

items.jp: 灰皿がもういっぱいだ

translation.pt-BR: O cinzeiro já está cheio.
translation.en: The ashtray is already full.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 灰皿 as the subject that is in the state of being full; here it presents the information as a new observation (the ashtray is full now).

items.jp: 庭の隅に小さい花が咲いた

translation.pt-BR: Uma florzinha desabrochou no canto do jardim.
translation.en: A little flower bloomed in the corner of the garden.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が presents 小さい花 as the new subject performing the action of blooming.

items.jp: 庭に猫が一匹いる

translation.pt-BR: Tem um gato no quintal.
translation.en: There's a cat in the backyard.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 猫 (cat) as the subject that exists; in existence sentences the being that 'there is' is marked by が.
tokens: numeral (part of the counter 一匹)

items.jp: 机の上に消しゴムがあります

translation.pt-BR: Tem uma borracha em cima da mesa.
translation.en: There's an eraser on the desk.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks the eraser as that which exists; it is the subject of あります.
tokens: part of the noun 消しゴム

items.jp: 指を切って、血が止まらない

translation.pt-BR: Cortei o dedo e o sangue não para de sair.
translation.en: I cut my finger and the bleeding won't stop.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 血 (blood) as the subject that does not stop, presenting it as new information.

items.jp: うちの猫は毛が長い

translation.pt-BR: O pelo do meu gato é comprido.
translation.en: My cat's fur is long.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 毛 (fur) as the specific aspect of the topic that receives the description 'is long'.

items.jp: 試験官がキョロキョロと周りを見た

translation.pt-BR: O fiscal olhou em volta, de um lado para o outro.
translation.en: The proctor looked around.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 試験官 ('the proctor') as the one who performs the action of looking around.

items.jp: 赤ちゃんって、肌が柔らかいんだよ。

translation.pt-BR: Bebê tem a pele macia, sabia?
translation.en: Babies have delicate skin.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca 肌 como o sujeito de 柔らかい, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: その地域で今、何が起きてるの？

translation.pt-BR: O que está acontecendo naquela região agora?
translation.en: What's going on in that area right now?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca 何 como o sujeito de 起きる, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: 再びベルが鳴りました。

translation.pt-BR: O sino tocou de novo.
translation.en: The bell rang again.

items.label: subject particle

items.jp: 国によって文化が違う

translation.pt-BR: A cultura varia de país para país.
translation.en: Culture varies from country to country.

items.label: connective particle (て form)
items.explanation: て closes the form 〜によって of よる, making it ready to introduce what varies according to the country.
tokens: verb of the phrase によって

items.jp: コーヒーを温かくしてもらえますか

translation.pt-BR: Você poderia esquentar o café para mim?
translation.en: Could you heat up the coffee for me?

items.label: connective particle (te-form)
items.explanation: て links して to もらえる, forming the structure 'do something + receive the favor' (〜てもらえる).

items.jp: 汚い手で食べてはいけません

translation.pt-BR: Não pode comer com as mãos sujas.
translation.en: You can't eat with dirty hands.

items.label: connective particle (te-form)
items.explanation: て links the verb 食べる to the following structure, forming 食べて, the mandatory base of the prohibition 〜てはいけません.

items.jp: 部屋をきれいにして、それから本を片付けた

translation.pt-BR: Deixei o quarto arrumadinho e depois guardei os livros.
translation.en: I tidied up the room and then put the books away.

items.label: connector て
items.explanation: て turns する into the て-form (して), chaining the first action to the second part of the sentence.

items.jp: 彼と競争して走った

translation.pt-BR: Apostei corrida com ele.
translation.en: I raced against him.

items.label: connective particle (te-form)
items.explanation: This て links the verb 競争する to the following verb 走る, chaining the two actions: 'compete and run'.
tokens: noun that forms the compound verb with する

items.jp: 指を切って、血が止まらない

translation.pt-BR: Cortei o dedo e o sangue não para de sair.
translation.en: I cut my finger and the bleeding won't stop.

items.label: connective particle (て form)
items.explanation: て links 切って to the second part, with the sense of 'and (as a consequence)'.

items.jp: 掃除をしてから出かける

translation.pt-BR: Vou fazer a limpeza e depois sair.
translation.en: I'll do the cleaning and then go out.

items.label: connective particle (て form)
items.explanation: て links し to から, forming the sequence してから ('after doing').
